title: Human action gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate human_action is the one gate a person finishes: entering their own password or credential, which the agent may not type. Its human_purpose must be password_entry; any other purpose refuses as human_action_misclassified and names the agent-run gate to use instead (machine_browser_approval, admission_owner_approval or admission_invite_entry). The contract refuses keys, ready_text, wait_seconds and any other field, so the step cannot type into the terminal or carry a secret; gate_timeout_seconds bounds the wait at 1..1800. The gate prints one machine_qa.operator_gate line with kind human_action, self_approving false, and instructions naming the step and where to type (the visible Terminal window or its tmux attach command); yoke watch qa-plan emits that line as urgent. It then only reads the terminal: completion_text passes; a denial or expiry fails as human_action_rejected; a setup exit fails as terminal_setup_exited; an expired wait fails as human_action_timed_out; a failed lease renewal fails as human_action_heartbeat_failed; each names a recovery. The step evidence records gate_evidence with the purpose, waited_seconds and self_approving false. The exploratory walker dispatch reserves WALK_STATUS: HUMAN_GATE for a password or credential entry the agent may not type; its report names that one entry and the resume state. Permission dialogs, sign-ins and approval codes belong to the agent or steering when they do not require prohibited credential entry.
